title: Cluster A — Kyiv–Western Border (P0777 vs P1480): DUPLICATE CONFIRMED, one system (КЗУ), combined length still unresolved

rows.recommendation: Fold into ONE surviving GEM row for the Kyiv–Western Border of Ukraine system (КЗУ). Do NOT keep P0777's 1,112.00 km / 522+590 km figures as-is — no source found ties those numbers to this corridor; GEM's own gem.wiki page for P0777 cites VTG (vtg.com.ua/experience/main/gts.html) for 522/590 km, but that page is now a genuine 404 (confirmed live: 'Stórinku ne znaideno') and its Wayback capture (20221216170410) is currently unreachable (persistent archive.org 503 across 6 attempts this session — an access failure, not proof of deletion; re-try later). Until VTG's figures can be independently re-verified, treat 522/590 as unsourced. Diameters (1020/1220 mm) and StartYear1 1970 are corroborated by other GEM-cited press (Interfax-Ukraine, eadaily.com, NGSI.ua) and by the independent operator-chronology account, so those attributes are solid; only the length pair is in question. If Update retains P0777 as the surviving PID (its name is the more standard rendering), its length/string fields need replacing, not preserving.
rows.notes: P0777 and P1480 share identical diameter pair (1020 mm + 1220 mm), identical corridor name family ('Kyiv–Western Border' variants), identical StartYear1 (1970), and both are recorded as two-string systems — the classic double-entry signature. No source located anywhere (uk.wikipedia, the general Ukraine-GTS wiki article, search engine snippets of utg.ua's own chronology page, kyiv.name local history, gem.wiki's own citation trails for both PIDs) describes a SECOND, competing 'Kyiv–Western border' gas system. Every named terminus fact for this name (Kam'yanka-Buzka on Dashava–Minsk for String I; Dolyna–Uzhhorod–State Border/'Bratstvo' for String II) appears exactly once, attached to one system, across every source. Route geometry: P0777's own drawn route is a bare 2-vertex schematic (near-Zhytomyr → Uzhhorod, ~356 km straight-line) which is far short of both circulating totals — consistent with a schematic lower bound, not evidence against either number.

rows.recommendation: Fold into the same single surviving row as P0777. P1480's length pair (183.6 + 216.3 = 399.90 km) IS traceable to a live citation trail — GEM's own P1480 gem.wiki page cites utg.ua's chronology page directly for exactly these numbers (retrieved 2022-08-26), and an independent Google-indexed snippet of what reads like the SAME utg.ua chronology text (found via targeted search, not via gem.wiki) reproduces '183.6 km, ∅1020mm... 216.3 km, ∅1220mm' verbatim-sounding language — so this pair is NOT baseless. However, a separate, independently-fetched Ukrainian Wikipedia article ALSO cites the same utg.ua chronology page and reports DIFFERENT numbers for the same two strings: 367 km and 506 km (total 873 km). Both citations point at the identical URL and give incompatible figures. The likeliest reconciliation (not confirmed — I could not open utg.ua directly to check) is that the chronology entry for 1970/1973 records an INITIAL commissioning length (183.6/216.3) that was later extended, with 367/506 representing the corridor's final built-out length after subsequent extension work also entered in the same chronology — i.e., two true readings of an evolving pipeline's length at different points in its build history, not two different pipelines. Recommend Update chase utg.ua's live chronology page directly once it stops 404ing/its Wayback capture stops 503ing (both are access failures this session, not deletions), and treat neither 399.9 nor 873 as settled until then. ALSO: correct/flag P1480's gem.wiki route narrative, which places its endpoint at 'Drozdovychi, Ukraine/Poland border' — this is UNCORROBORATED and almost certainly a conflation. Drozdovychi is the named terminus of a wholly separate, smaller-diameter corridor (Komarno–Drozdovychi, historically 520/720 mm per an independent uk.wikipedia article on that specific corridor, now GEM's own P0778 at 800 mm/80 km) and is also the name attached to a modern Poland–Ukraine interconnector expansion project (the 'Drozdovychi-Bilche-Volytsya' investment scheme tied to the Świnoujście LNG-to-CEE build-out) — either of which is a plausible source of the error. P1480's sheet EndLocation is blank, so this is a caveat for Update to resolve when it sets EndLocation on the surviving row, not a live sheet error today.
rows.notes: P1480's own drawn route (3-vertex: Kyiv → near Ternopil → ~22.9°E/49.68°N, a point west of Lviv near the Polish border, NOT Uzhhorod) diverges geometrically from P0777's drawn route (which ends at Uzhhorod) — and this drawn route's own span (~561 km) already EXCEEDS P1480's stated 399.9 km, which is the 'schematic exceeds stated' signature the brief flags as meaningful (not just a shortfall). That drawn divergence toward the Polish border rather than Uzhhorod is circumstantial support for how the Drozdovychi mislabeling crept in (a researcher schematizing 'western border' picked a different plausible western crossing than Uzhhorod), but per the discipline rule this is a hypothesis about an ERROR IN DRAWING, not evidence of a second physical pipeline — no textual source anywhere describes a Kyiv-to-Poland-border trunk distinct from the Kyiv–Kamianka-Buzka–Dolyna–Uzhhorod КЗУ system.

summary: P0777 and P1480 are DUPLICATE_CONFIRMED: both describe the single Soviet-era 'Kyiv–Western Border of Ukraine' gas transmission system (КЗУ), not two distinct pipelines. The identity case rests on more than structural resemblance: no source found anywhere — across a dedicated uk.wikipedia article, the general Ukraine-GTS wiki article, search-engine-indexed fragments of utg.ua's own chronology, local Kyiv-region history writing, and both PIDs' own gem.wiki citation trails — describes a second, competing 'Kyiv–Western border' corridor. Every distinctive terminus fact attached to this name (a northward String I to Kam'yanka-Buzka on the Dashava–Minsk route, feeding Belarus/the Baltics and, in reverse, Poland; a southwestward String II via Ternopil into the Dolyna–Uzhhorod–State Border 'Bratstvo' system) appears exactly once in the literature, attached to one system, with both strings sharing one corridor from Kyiv/Boyarka to Ternopil before splitting. Both GEM rows carry the identical 1020mm+1220mm diameter pair, identical StartYear1 (1970), and an identical two-string structure — the double-entry signature this project treats as a hypothesis, here corroborated (not refuted, unlike the comparable Kazakh cluster) by the total absence of any competing sourced identity. GEM's own P1480 endpoint claim of 'Drozdovychi' is a separate, traceable error: an independent uk.wikipedia article on the Komarno–Drozdovychi corridor documents that crossing as a wholly different, smaller-diameter (520/720mm historically) system, and the general Ukraine-GTS article lists Uzhhorod and Drozdovychi as two DIFFERENT named border points — so the Drozdovychi attribution on P1480's gem.wiki page is unsupported and likely conflates this corridor with GEM's own separate P0778 (Komarno–Drozdovychi) and/or a modern Poland interconnector expansion project of similar name. What remains genuinely unresolved is WHICH length figure survives the fold. Three totals circulate — P0777's 1,112.00 km (522+590, sourced by GEM to a now-dead VTG page I could independently confirm is 404, with its Wayback capture unreachable all session), P1480's 399.90 km (183.6+216.3, which GEM cites directly to utg.ua's chronology, and which an independent search-engine snippet of what appears to be that same chronology page's own wording corroborates almost verbatim), and Wikipedia's 873 km (367+506, ALSO cited to the identical utg.ua chronology URL). Two derivative sources thus name the SAME primary document for two incompatible numbers, and I could not adjudicate between them because utg.ua's live page 404s and its Wayback capture 503'd on every one of 11 attempts across this session — a documented access failure, not evidence either figure is wrong. My working (unconfirmed) hypothesis is that 183.6/216.3 is the pipeline's INITIAL 1970/1973 commissioning length and 367/506 is a later cumulative/extended figure recorded further down the same chronology, i.e. two true readings of one system's build history rather than a contradiction — but Update should chase utg.ua directly (and the Nazarenko dissertation, also unreachable this session) before committing to a number, rather than trusting either derivative reading.
